details:
Q1. The re-plan cannot start unless the issue's label changes first. How should that happen, given the "no new gh API call" constraint?
Choices:
A. Allow exactly one extra call, only on the eligible re-plan path: one `gh issue edit` that adds `ai:planning` and removes `ai:awaiting-approval`, made before the `/answer` comment. If that edit fails, skip the re-plan and post today's hold notice instead. If the comment fails after the edit, the issue sits in `ai:planning`, where the existing `retrigger_plan` stall arm picks it up. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Same single extra call, but only add `ai:planning` and leave `ai:awaiting-approval` in place (plan.yml checks `ai:planning` first). Downside: the issue briefly carries two phase labels until plan.yml moves it back to `ai:awaiting-approval`.
C. Make no label call from the poller. Instead, change plan.yml's trigger check to also accept `ai:awaiting-approval` when the `/answer` comment carries the `ai:automation-path-replan:v1` marker. This moves part of the recovery into `plan.yml`, against the "recovery happens in the poller only" non-goal.
D. Keep "no new gh API call" strict and drop the automatic re-plan. Only the `replannable` field and a log line ship; the hold notice still goes to a human. This does not meet the issue's main goal.
